Reading the structure region by region:

- **Indazole fragment:** a 1H-indazole bearing the amide NH at C3 and a 3,5-difluorobenzyl group at C5.
- **Central benzamide:** C(=O)NH joins the indazole to a benzene ring. Ortho to the carbonyl is NH-(tetrahydropyran-4-yl). Para to the carbonyl is a piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine and azetidine:** the piperidine C4 carries an azetidine N. The azetidine C3 bears an isoindolinone aryl group.
- **Isoindolinone:** the aryl is attached at C5 of the isoindolinone. The lactam nitrogen carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

Indazole SMILES: c1(NC(=O)...)n[nH]c2ccc(Cc3cc(F)cc(F)c3)cc12

Benzamide ring: C(=O) at position 1, NH-THP at position 2, piperidine N at position 4. Written from the carbonyl carbon: c1(C(=O)N...)ccc(N2CCC(CC2)N2CC(C2)...)cc1NC1CCOCC1

Isoindolinone: c5ccc6C(=O)N(Cc6c5)C7CCC(=O)NC7=O, with the azetidine attached at c5.

Full SMILES:
O=C(Nc1n[nH]c2ccc(Cc3cc(F)cc(F)c3)cc12)c1ccc(cc1NC1CCOCC1)N1CCC(CC1)N1CC(C1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(Cc2c1)C1CCC(=O)NC1=O

Ring-closure check: the indazole ring label 1 is closed at "cc12", where 2 closes the benzo ring and 1 closes the pyrazole. Label 1 is then reused for the benzamide ring, and the THP ring opens and closes within "NC1CCOCC1" while the benzamide label 1 is still open. That is a conflict, so I renumber.

Benzamide: c4ccc(cc4NC5CCOCC5)N6CCC(CC6)N7CC(C7)c8ccc9C(=O)N(Cc9c8)C%10CCC(=O)NC%10=O

The benzamide ring (label 4) closes at "cc4", after which the NH-THP substituent hangs from that last atom. In "c4ccc(cc4NC5CCOCC5)N6...", the atom "c4" closes the ring and then bears the NH, so the NH is on the ring-closing atom, which is adjacent to the first atom (the carbonyl-bearing carbon). The piperidine N is on the 4th atom, para to the first. This is correct.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1n[nH]c2ccc(Cc3cc(F)cc(F)c3)cc12)c4ccc(cc4NC5CCOCC5)N6CCC(CC6)N7CC(C7)c8ccc9C(=O)N(Cc9c8)C%10CCC(=O)NC%10=O
